reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Strong evidence of target engagement - IL-12 mRNA expression increased up to 162,946-fold in tumors with vector copy numbers up to 140,000,000 copies per 100ng DNA, confirming the gene therapy vector successfully delivered and expressed IL-12. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: Clear downstream biology changes - IFN-gamma mRNA increased up to 417-fold and CD8+ T-cell percentages modestly increased, confirming IL-12-mediated immune activation occurred as intended. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: This was a Phase I dose-escalation trial with safety as the primary endpoint, which was met with MTD established at 160mg/day. Secondary efficacy signals showed partial responses with ORR 7.7% and median PFS 64 days, which are encouraging for a Phase I trial in melanoma. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analysis reported in this dose-escalation study. 5. CONFOUNDERS: While there were significant toxicities (53.8% Grade 3+ AEs), the MTD was successfully established and the trial achieved its primary safety objectives. The efficacy signals, while modest, are appropriate for a Phase I study and support further development.

failure_modes.evidence: 53.8% of patients experienced Grade 3+ drug-related adverse events at higher doses, with dose-limiting toxicities including pancytopenia and mental status changes requiring dose modifications in Phase II portion
